title: Concept of Anomie in Modern Societies
text:
Anomie, a concept originally popularized by Émile Durkheim, describes a state of normlessness within a society. This condition arises when social regulations weaken or change rapidly, leaving individuals without clear guidelines for behavior or emotional direction.

The lack of established social norms can lead to feelings of detachment and aimlessness among the population. In periods of intense industrialization or rapid cultural shifts, traditional moral structures may break down faster than new ones can be implemented, thereby eroding collective cohesion.

Understanding anomie suggests that societal stability relies not merely on physical infrastructure, but fundamentally on a robust, shared framework of rules and expected behaviors.
